correctness.rationale: Two distinct edges cannot share both endpoints. A violating triple therefore has a left-sharing pair and a different right-sharing pair, so it is precisely a three-edge path. The resulting star forest is saturated if it spans, since any missing edge between nontrivial components makes a path. If it has a left isolate, a right isolate would permit an added edge, and every right vertex must be a leaf of a left-centered star of degree at least two; these conditions also suffice. The other orientation is symmetric. Spanning components contribute H(x,y); k spanning components give exactly 2q-k edges. The q!/(q-k)! factor assigns unlabeled leaf blocks to distinct labeled centers, and all nonspanning families have q edges. Two opposite stars and k-2 separate edges realize every size, with both stars regarded as separate edges in the matching case. At the maximum there are two opposite stars of degree q-1 and their centers determine the forest, giving q². This checks q=3 and the full range q>=3, with no quotient by label permutations.
residual_risks: The bounded independent enumeration does not check q>=5; the all-q result uses the structural proof, not the computation.

evidence: The rook-graph spanning EGF exponent is the edge-weighted H; on taking q vertices on each side a term with k components has weight z^(2q-k). Expansion of the exponential thus yields the exact spanning term, and the two matching isolate terms yield the remaining coefficient at q. The two-star construction, maximum coefficient and interpolation of sizes also follow immediately from the same classification. Shangguan–Ge's cited construction gives 2q-2, but their Theorem 1.5 alone gives a generic 2q bound here; the older saturation-game material is structural and extremal, not a labeled terminal polynomial.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The main finding and consequences are a mechanical square specialization of the distinct Resultary theorem. The older extremal literature by itself would not establish this complete overlap.

evidence: Rook cells are the same labeled pairs. For nonadjacent cells, the two cross cells are the only possible internal vertices of their geodesics. With at least one endpoint selected, failure of outer-mutual visibility requires the two cross cells selected too, exhibiting exactly a selected three-edge path. Every such path gives a failure. The hash condition forbids precisely these paths.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The identity on selected cells gives a size-preserving bijection of admissible families and preserves inclusion and maximality, not just the extreme sizes.
